# Reference {#sec-reference}

This guide covers common tasks. The cuPhoton repository holds the full reference: each module's options, data contracts and limits, the command-line index and troubleshooting. This page lists where each part lives. The links point to the repository's `main` branch, which can be newer than this guide.

## Command line

`cuphoton --help` lists the command groups, one per module:

```{python}
#| echo: false
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

cli = Path(sys.executable).with_name("cuphoton")
print(subprocess.run([str(cli), "--help"], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.strip())
```

`cuphoton <group> --help` lists a group's commands, and `cuphoton <group> help <command>` prints one command's options with their defaults. The [command-line index](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cuPhoton/blob/main/docs/cli.md) describes every group. @sec-concepts explains the flags that the groups share.

## Python API

Each function's docstring documents its arguments, defaults and return fields. Print a signature with `inspect`, or the whole docstring with `help`:

```{python}
import inspect
from cuphoton.xrep import reproject_masked_array

print(inspect.signature(reproject_masked_array))
```

Each package lists its public names in `__all__`:

```{python}
import importlib

print("package          public names")
for name in ("core", "xdr", "xrep", "ximage", "xpois", "xfit", "xscan", "xray", "xbeam", "xlens"):
    package = importlib.import_module(f"cuphoton.{name}")
    print(f"cuphoton.{name:7s} {len(package.__all__):12d}")
```

xScan and xRay export only their version at the top level. They are command-line tools first. Their reference pages show the submodules to import from, such as `cuphoton.xscan.fits_inference` and `cuphoton.xray.detector_artifacts`. Core's shared code also lives in submodules:

- `cuphoton.core.fits_io`: the FITS reader and its receipts.
- `cuphoton.core.arrays`: helpers that serve NumPy and CuPy arrays with one code path.
- `cuphoton.core.cli`: the command-line framework.
- `cuphoton.core.executors`: Dragon and MPI execution.

- [Getting started](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cuPhoton/blob/main/docs/getting-started.md): install profiles and platform notes.

- [Glossary](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cuPhoton/blob/main/docs/glossary.md): cuPhoton and astronomy terms.

## Getting help

cuPhoton has best-effort community support through its GitHub repository. Its [support policy](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cuPhoton/blob/main/SUPPORT.md) gives the details.

1. Search the [GitHub issues](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cuPhoton/issues) for your problem.
2. If no issue matches, open a bug report with a minimal reproducer. Include the following:
   - the output of `cuphoton --version`
   - the cuPhoton commit, Python version, operating system and installed extras
   - the command line and the shapes of your inputs
   - for a GPU problem, the GPU model, driver, CUDA runtime, the backend from `summary.json`, and whether the CPU profile works
3. Open a feature request for a new workflow or data contract, or a pull request for a concrete fix.

Remove credentials, private paths and proprietary data from what you post. Do not report security problems on GitHub. Follow the [security policy](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cuPhoton/blob/main/SECURITY.md) instead.
